Phonetic punctuation

Ceolachan
did you WRITE phonetic punctuation? I must admit it must be somewhat difficult to write.

Do you know p-language?
The simple rule are as follows: say the first syllable, repeat with a P in the beginning of the syllable, say the second syllable, repeat with a P in the beginning, and so forth.
Ex: I think sheetmusic is only a shadow of music played in a session=
Ipi thinkpink sheetpeetmupusicpic ispis onponlypy apa shapadowpow ofpof mupusicpic playedplayed inpin apa sespessionpion.
OK?
;-)

Hey Johnny Cope, X:5

This version is an almost exact transcription of what NM is actually playing. I have studied and analyzed the tune intensely - slowed the music down, listened, played along, written down - and this is the result. I have left out various ornaments, though. Hope you find it useful anyway 🙂

PS. The ABC-file posted earlier is unfortunately corrupted!

↳ Posted by fingelin on December 7th, 2022.

Johnny Cope, traditional Scots march, X:6

Kathryn Tickell’s setting on fiddle from On Kielder Side, mostly played without dotted eighths except lightly in the second part. Otherwise similar to Natalie MacMaster’s, except note the 2/4 bar in the first part where two beats have been omitted.

As documented by Nicholas Brown on the rushymountain link cited above, this tune is greatly older than the commonly played 6-part Irish hornpipe Johnny Cope (in A dorian), which seems to have morphed mysteriously from this one under the bow of Padraig O’Keefe and thence spread widely.

Played in G minor (2 flats) and with those solemn G octaves rounding out each variation, this is just a GRAND TUNE by any measure. Yet it’s stuck in here with the wrong name and tune type and exhibits on just a handful of recordings. Go figure.
